name: Nebraska Environmental Trust grants
summary: Lottery-funded grants for projects in Nebraska under five categories (habitat, water, waste, air, soil); the habitat category covers preserving and restoring native habitat and at-risk species. Open to individuals, private organisations and public entities, with an application round each year.

steps: Online application and signed signature page
Public hearing, then Board award vote

eligibility.rule: Does not pay for land or easements acquired without the full consent of the landowner
Does not provide direct assistance to regulatory programs
Does not implement actions mandated by regulations, except remediation
Does not pay for private benefits or primarily private-benefit projects
Does not relieve private environmental liability, except soil or groundwater remediation

documents: Current annual budget summary, if a government agency
Current-year operating budget, if a not-for-profit or for-profit organization
Most recent Form 990 tax return, if a not-for-profit organization
Most recent profit/loss statement, if a for-profit organization
Funding partner letter of support, if applicable
Aerial photo of the property, if requesting real estate funding
Legal description of the property, if requesting real estate funding
Site plan for the real estate project, if applicable
Detailed plans, profiles or cross-sections, if a restoration or improvement project
Landowner letter, if restoring or improving property the sponsor does not own

status.quote: Applications will be accepted until Tuesday, September 8, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CDT.

opens.quote: The Nebraska Environmental Trust (NET) grant cycle for funding year 2027 will open for applications on Monday, July 13, 2026.

deadline.quote: Applications will be accepted until Tuesday, September 8, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CDT.

applicant_types.quote: Individuals, private organizations, and public entities may apply. For-profit organizations must demonstrate that the project results in public benefit and does not pay for private benefits.

geography.quote: The Nebraska Environmental Trust is established to conserve, enhance, and restore the natural environments of Nebraska.

access.quote: All applications must be submitted through the Nebraska Environmental Trust online grant application portal

window.quote: The Nebraska Environmental Trust accepts grant applications annually. Applications open around July and are due on or before the first Tuesday after Labor Day in September.

co_finance_required.quote: A match is not required in any amount or percentage.

effort.quote: The signature page will be available to print, sign, and scan when all sections of the application are completed.
The list is published, and a public hearing is scheduled, after which the board votes to issue awards.

eligibility.quote: Will this project pay for land or easements acquired without the full and express consent of the landowner?
Does your project provide direct assistance to regulatory programs?
Does your project implement actions mandated by regulations, excluding remediation?
Will your project pay for private benefits or provide assistance to projects or portions of projects whose benefits are primarily private in nature?

Will your project relieve private liability for environmental damage (except for projects for remediation of soils or ground water) or provide assistance to projects in order to relieve such liability?
Does your project offer public benefits?
Is your project financially and technically feasible?

after_award.quote: a. Quarterly Reports. The Sponsor agrees to file such statements and reports according to the following schedule:

documents.quote: Provide current annual budget summary. Not-For-Profit Organizations - Provide the operating budget for the current year and most recent Form 990 Tax Return. For-Profit Organizations - Provide operating budget for the current year, and most recent profit/loss statement.
Any Partner contributing to the project will need to provide a letter of support.
include an aerial photo of the property and legal description
Site Plan that shows the legal boundary of site, existing features and structures, and proposed structures and improvements.

Attach detailed plans, profiles, or cross-sections to show that the structures will be designed in accordance with any applicable regulations, codes, or standard practices, and to allow reasonable estimation of cost.
If restoration of, or improvements to, property not owned by the sponsor(s), attach a letter from the landowner(s) confirming participation in the project.
